subject: Approval needed: HealthMetrics special pricing (VP/CFO sign-off)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Approval needed: HealthMetrics special pricing (VP/CFO sign-off)

Team — I need a quick internal approval path for HealthMetrics. Negotiations finished last night; customer has agreed to a 12-month commitment but we had to concede on price to win against two competitors. Commercial ask: approve a 40% first-year discount on list for the platform + waive onboarding professional services fees (~$40k).

High-level rationale:
- HealthMetrics is a strategic account in the digital health space with strong case study potential and reference value.
- Expected ARR after year 1: $980k (with upsell potential into observability).
- Competitor pressure: they indicated they would go to both competitor X and Y if we don’t move.
- Legal/PO timeline: they want terms and signature within 48 hours to align with board approval.

Attachments: HM_SOW_v1.pdf, pricing_breakdown.xlsx (I attached the proposed numbers). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

I know 40% is outside our standard authority — requesting VP/CFO sign-off (Rachel). Aditya, can you confirm margin impact and whether a credit alternative makes sense? Monica, I’ll need a short exception memo for Rachel to sign (one page + finance table).

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval needed: HealthMetrics special pricing (VP/CFO sign-off)

Thanks Marcus — quick context from the customer call: they have an urgent migration window starting in May and will put our platform in the pilot across 3 clinical teams immediately. They published a procurement budget for year 1 that is constrained, hence pushing hard on price.

I support a commercial concession but prefer a structure to protect net revenue: propose 30% off list + $100k in platform credits that vest over 6 months instead of a straight 40% off. That preserves list pricing visibility and gives us levers for usage.

If we go to 40% off list, I recommend we require a 12-month committed ARR plus a small implementation fee (we waive PS but bill a token implementation admin fee).

I can draft the one-page exception memo and the customer-facing language. Marcus — can you loop in HealthMetrics legal to confirm they’ll accept our standard redlines?

—Monica
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Approval needed: HealthMetrics special pricing (VP/CFO sign-off)

Marcus/Monica — ran the numbers and attached a short analysis (financials_analysis.xlsx). Summary:
- Current list revenue (12 months) = $1,300,000.
- 40% discount reduces cash collected to $780,000 (loss vs list = $520,000).
- With onboarding waiver, net revenue drops further (~$480k net reduction in year 1).
- Gross margin impact: would push the deal below our target threshold for a standard enterprise sale.

Recommendation: authorize up to 30% off list at finance level. Anything above 30% should get VP/CFO approval. If you want to reach equivalent economic value without a straight discount, consider:
  - $100k platform credits amortized over first 6 months (less immediate cash impact)
  - Stage-based true-ups: additional revenue targets post-pilot that convert credits to billable usage

If the board/exec value of the reference is high and legal timelines demand speed, I can make an exception recommendation to Rachel, but will need the one-page memo that outlines strategic value, net present value and controls (audit clause, usage audit, termination triggers).

-Aditya
Finance Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Aditya — appreciate the analysis. Quick commercial counterpoints:
- HealthMetrics has named product references and several pilot advocates who will drive cross-team rollouts. Losing the deal likely means they sign with competitor X and be unavailable as a reference.
- The margin loss in year 1 is real, but we expect >2x expansion in year 2 from usage-driven add-ons.
- Procurement has a strong timeline: if we miss the 48-hour window we drop to the back of their vendor list.

Given the time sensitivity and the strategic nature, I’m escalating for Rachel’s review. I’ve included a one-page memo (attached) that summarizes the strategic case and the proposed controls (audit rights, mandatory quarterly business reviews, and rollback clause if usage < 25% of committed).

If Rachel wants an alternative, propose: 35% + $50k credits and a mandatory 9-month review with performance milestones. But our ask remains 40% + PS waiver.

Marcus
Account Exec — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Approval needed: HealthMetrics special pricing (VP/CFO sign-off)

Thanks for the clear write-ups and numbers. I reviewed the analysis; I’m sympathetic to the strategic rationale but need to balance short-term margin with precedent risk.

Decision outline:
- Approve the special pricing under the following conditions: either (A) 35% off list + $75k platform credits amortized over 3 quarters, OR (B) 40% off list only if HealthMetrics commits to a 24-month minimum term (paid annually) and we include a clawback clause tied to usage metrics.
- We will not waive all onboarding fees — approve a capped implementation credit of $15k (not a full waiver).
- Require the one-page exception memo with finance table (Marcus) and a short legal addendum describing the audit and termination rights.

Next steps: Marcus, please finalize the memo reflecting option A and B; get HealthMetrics to indicate which option they prefer. Legal will need to review redlines before I sign. I’m happy to sign once legal and revenue ops confirm the controls.

Rachel Kim
CFO, Redwood Inference
